key_insight: ReScene4D formalizes temporally sparse 4D semantic instance segmentation and shows that maintaining consistent instance identities across intermittently captured 3D scans—despite unobserved changes—is both a distinct task and solvable with joint segmentation + temporal association.
problem_solved: Existing 3D semantic instance segmentation methods break when indoor scenes evolve between sporadic scans; this work addresses how to segment, identify, and temporally associate object instances across time-varying, intermittently observed 3D data.
method: Define the temporally sparse 4D SIS task and provide an evaluation protocol that measures segmentation, identity persistence, and temporal association across scans.

Introduce ReScene4D (dataset/benchmark) of evolving indoor scenes captured intermittently and use joint segmentation-and-association models that combine geometric and semantic cues to propagate instance identities over time.
Evaluate and benchmark baseline methods, highlighting failure modes of per-scan 3DSIS and demonstrating improvements from explicitly modeling temporal consistency.
impact: Provides a realistic benchmark and clear evaluation for long-term scene understanding in robotics, AR/VR, and scene monitoring; enables practitioners to build models that reliably track objects across sparse, real-world 3D observations.

paper_title: ReScene4D: Temporally Consistent Semantic Instance Segmentation of Evolving Indoor 3D Scenes
paper_authors: Emily Steiner, Jianhao Zheng, Henry Howard-Jenkins, Chris Xie, Iro Armeni
